The SI unit of specific heat capacity is J kg–1
What is the unit of specific heat capacity expressed in SI base units?
A
m s–2
K–1
B
kg m s–1 K–1
C
m2
s–2
K–1
D
kg m2
s–1
K–1

hints: Start from the given $\text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$ and first replace the joule using energy as force times distance, $\text{J} = \text{N m}$.
Replace the newton with SI base units using $F = ma$, so $\text{N} = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$ and therefore $\text{J} = \text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$.
Multiply by $\text{kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$ and cancel the $\text{kg}$ terms, leaving $\text{K}^{-1}$ unchanged, then check the powers of $\text{m}$ and $\text{s}$.
walkthrough: Write the starting unit: specific heat capacity has unit $\text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.
Express the joule in terms of newton and metre: $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$.
Express the newton in SI base units from $F = ma$: $1 \text{ N} = 1 \text{ kg m s}^{-2}$, so $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$.

A.explanation: This has only $\text{m}^1$ and is the base-unit form of $\text{J kg}^{-1}\text{m}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$, not $\text{J kg}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: The $\text{kg}$ should cancel with $\text{kg}^{-1}$ and the power of $\text{s}$ should be $-2$, so $\text{kg m s}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$ cannot be correct.

C.explanation: Since $\text{J} = \text{kg m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}$, dividing by $\text{kg}$ and $\text{K}$ leaves $\text{m}^2\text{ s}^{-2}\text{K}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: This keeps an extra $\text{kg}$ and uses $\text{s}^{-1}$; the joule contributes $\text{s}^{-2}$ and its $\text{kg}$ cancels with $\text{kg}^{-1}$.
